title: What is Agentic AI? | IBM
summary: IBM defines agentic AI as an autonomous AI system that accomplishes goals with limited supervision, building on generative AI and large language models to act independently through coordinated AI agents.

entities.name: Agentic AI
entities.evidence: IBM defines agentic AI as an AI system that can accomplish specific goals with limited supervision, exhibiting autonomy, goal-driven behavior, and adaptability through AI agents.

entities.name: Generative AI
entities.evidence: The article describes generative AI as the technology that agentic AI builds upon, focusing on creating content based on learned patterns rather than autonomous action.

entities.name: Large Language Models
entities.evidence: The article identifies LLMs as the reasoning engines that agentic AI uses to function in dynamic environments and make decisions.

entities.name: AI Agents
entities.evidence: AI agents are described as machine learning models that mimic human decision-making to solve problems in real time, forming the core components of agentic AI systems.

entities.name: AI Orchestration
entities.evidence: The article mentions AI orchestration as the coordination mechanism that manages the efforts of multiple AI agents working together in a multiagent system.

relations.explanation: Agentic AI builds on generative AI techniques by using large language models to function in dynamic environments, extending content generation toward autonomous goal pursuit.
Agentic AI uses large language models as reasoning engines to accomplish goals, applying their generative capabilities toward specific tasks with limited supervision.
AI agents are machine learning models—often built on large language models—that mimic human decision-making to solve problems in real time.
In a multiagent system, individual AI agents performing specific subtasks have their efforts coordinated through AI orchestration.
